questions.q: Which country do tacos come from?
questions.fact: Tacos were eaten in Mexico long before the Spanish arrived, often filled with small fish.

questions.q: Kimchi, a spicy fermented cabbage dish, is a national food of which country?
questions.fact: Many Korean families make big batches of kimchi together in late autumn, a tradition called kimjang.

questions.q: Which country does the stir-fried noodle dish pad thai come from?
questions.fact: Pad thai became popular in Thailand in the 1930s and 1940s.

questions.q: Which country is famous for pho, a noodle soup with broth and herbs?
questions.fact: Pho is often eaten for breakfast in Vietnam.

questions.q: Which country is famous for fish and chips?
questions.fact: Fish and chips were so important in Britain that they were not rationed during World War II.

questions.q: Which country is famous for haggis, made with sheep's heart, liver and lungs?
questions.fact: Haggis is traditionally eaten on Burns Night, January 25.

questions.q: Poutine, fries topped with cheese curds and gravy, comes from which country?
questions.fact: Poutine was first served in the province of Quebec in the 1950s.

questions.q: Pierogi, filled dumplings, are a famous food of which country?
questions.fact: Pierogi can be filled with potato, cheese, cabbage, meat or even fruit.

questions.q: Goulash, a stew seasoned with paprika, comes from which country?
questions.fact: Goulash was first cooked by Hungarian cattle herders in big kettles over open fires.

questions.q: Moussaka, a baked dish of eggplant and meat, is famous in which country?
questions.fact: Greek moussaka is usually topped with a thick, creamy white sauce.

questions.q: Which crispy fried balls made from chickpeas or fava beans are popular across the Middle East?
questions.fact: Falafel is often stuffed inside pita bread with salad and tahini sauce.

questions.q: Which noodle soup is hugely popular in Japan but first came from China?
questions.fact: Japan has a museum all about ramen in Yokohama.

questions.q: What is the name of the small Chinese dishes, like dumplings and buns, often served with tea?
questions.fact: Dim sum is a big part of Cantonese food from southern China.

questions.q: Which famous roast duck dish is named after China's capital?
questions.fact: Peking is an old spelling of Beijing.

questions.q: What is the thin, dried seaweed used to wrap sushi rolls called?
questions.fact: Nori is made by pressing seaweed into thin sheets, a bit like making paper.

questions.q: What is most of the green "wasabi" served with sushi outside Japan actually made from?
questions.fact: Real wasabi is a rare plant that is hard to grow, so most restaurants use horseradish colored green.

questions.q: What is tempura?
choices: Food dipped in light batter and deep-fried
questions.fact: Portuguese traders and missionaries are thought to have brought the idea of tempura to Japan in the 1500s.

questions.q: What is miso made from?
questions.fact: Miso soup is eaten at many Japanese breakfasts.

questions.q: What are edamame?
questions.fact: Edamame are often boiled in their pods with salt and popped out to eat.

questions.q: Which Korean dish is a bowl of rice topped with vegetables, meat, an egg and chili paste, all mixed together?
questions.fact: Bibimbap means "mixed rice" in Korean.

questions.q: Which Peruvian dish is made of raw fish "cooked" in lime or lemon juice?
questions.fact: The acid in citrus juice changes the fish's proteins, a little like heat does.

questions.q: Which black bean and pork stew is a national dish of Brazil?
questions.fact: Feijoada is often served on Saturdays in Brazil with rice, greens and orange slices.

questions.q: Which corn cakes are a daily food in Venezuela and Colombia?
questions.fact: Arepas can be grilled, baked or fried and split open to hold fillings.

questions.q: Which fried dough sticks, often dipped in hot chocolate, are a classic treat in Spain?
questions.fact: In Spain, churros and chocolate are a popular breakfast.

questions.q: What is the name for small Spanish dishes shared as snacks or a meal?
questions.fact: Tapa means "lid" or "cover" in Spanish, and one story says bars covered drinks with a slice of bread.

questions.q: Which cold tomato soup comes from southern Spain?
questions.fact: Gazpacho is a refreshing summer soup from Andalusia.

questions.q: Which fermented cabbage dish is especially popular in Germany?
questions.fact: Sauerkraut means "sour cabbage" in German.

questions.q: Which country is famous for cheese fondue, where you dip bread into melted cheese?
questions.fact: Tradition says if you drop your bread in the fondue pot, you have to do a silly forfeit.

questions.q: Which long, thin French bread was added to UNESCO's list of cultural heritage in 2022?
questions.fact: French bakeries make billions of baguettes each year.

questions.q: What are thin French pancakes called?
questions.fact: Savory buckwheat crêpes from Brittany are often called galettes.

questions.q: What are escargots, a famous French dish?
questions.fact: Escargots are usually cooked with garlic, butter and parsley.

questions.q: Which vegetable stew from the south of France shares its name with a Pixar movie?
questions.fact: Ratatouille usually has eggplant, zucchini, peppers, tomatoes and onions.

questions.q: Which creamy Italian rice dish is stirred slowly while adding broth?
questions.fact: Risotto is made with short-grain rice like Arborio, which releases starch to make it creamy.

questions.q: What does the name of the Italian dessert tiramisu mean?
questions.fact: Tiramisu has coffee-soaked biscuits, which may be where the "pick me up" name comes from.

questions.q: Which green Italian sauce is made from basil, pine nuts, garlic, cheese and olive oil?
questions.fact: Pesto comes from Genoa, and its name comes from an Italian word for pounding.

questions.q: Traditional mozzarella di bufala is made from the milk of which animal?
questions.fact: Water buffalo milk has more fat than cow's milk, which makes the cheese very creamy.

questions.q: Which famous hard Italian cheese has the full name Parmigiano-Reggiano?
questions.fact: Wheels of Parmigiano-Reggiano weigh around 40 kilograms each.

questions.q: Pizza Margherita is said to be named after which person?
questions.fact: Its red tomato, white mozzarella and green basil match the colors of the Italian flag.

questions.q: Which salty white cheese, often made from sheep's milk, is famous in Greece?
questions.fact: Feta is stored in salty water called brine to keep it fresh.

questions.q: Which Greek dip is made from yogurt, cucumber and garlic?
questions.fact: Tzatziki is often served with grilled meat and pita bread.

questions.q: Which sweet pastry is made from layers of thin dough, chopped nuts and honey or syrup?
questions.fact: Baklava was a famous treat in the kitchens of the Ottoman sultans.

questions.q: What is the meat roasted on a tall turning spit and shaved off in thin slices for wraps called in the Middle East?
questions.fact: Similar dishes are called döner kebab in Turkey and gyros in Greece.

questions.q: Couscous, a staple of North Africa, is made from what?
questions.fact: Couscous is steamed rather than boiled in traditional North African cooking.

questions.q: What is the cone-shaped clay pot used to cook slow stews in Morocco called?
questions.fact: The cone shape lets steam rise, cool and drip back down to keep food moist.

questions.q: Which spicy tomato rice dish is a favorite across West Africa, with friendly rivalry between Ghana and Nigeria?
questions.fact: Fans in Ghana and Nigeria argue playfully about which country makes the best jollof.

questions.q: What spongy flatbread from Ethiopia is used as both a plate and a spoon?
questions.fact: Injera is made from teff, a tiny grain that grows in the Ethiopian highlands.

questions.q: Which dark, salty spread made from yeast extract is an Australian favorite?
questions.fact: Vegemite was created in 1922, and Australians usually spread it very thinly on toast.

questions.q: Which meringue dessert with fruit on top is claimed by both Australia and New Zealand?
questions.fact: It was named after the Russian ballerina Anna Pavlova.

questions.q: Which Indian rice dish is cooked in layers with spices and often meat?
questions.fact: Biryani is often flavored with saffron, which turns some of the rice golden.

questions.q: What is naan?
choices: A flatbread baked in a clay oven
questions.fact: Naan dough is slapped onto the hot inside wall of a clay oven called a tandoor.

questions.q: What is a samosa?
choices: A fried pastry filled with spiced potatoes or meat
questions.fact: Samosas are usually shaped like triangles.

questions.q: What are bagels boiled in water before?
questions.fact: Boiling gives bagels their shiny, chewy crust.

questions.q: Which German city is the frankfurter sausage named after?
questions.fact: Hot dogs in the United States grew out of the frankfurter.

questions.q: Buffalo wings were first made in which US city?
questions.fact: Buffalo wings are said to have been first served at the Anchor Bar in 1964.

questions.q: Which US city is famous for cheesesteak sandwiches?
questions.fact: A Philly cheesesteak has thin slices of beef with melted cheese on a long roll.

questions.q: Which US city is famous for deep-dish pizza?
questions.fact: Deep-dish pizza is baked in a tall pan, with the sauce often on top of the cheese.

questions.q: Which thick stew from Louisiana is often made with okra, shrimp and sausage?
questions.fact: Gumbo may come from a West African word for okra.

questions.q: Who invented nachos in 1943?
questions.fact: Nachos were named after their inventor, whose nickname was Nacho.

questions.q: In which country was the Caesar salad invented?
questions.fact: Restaurant owner Caesar Cardini is said to have created it in Tijuana in 1924.

questions.q: Who invented the chocolate chip cookie in the 1930s?
questions.fact: Ruth Wakefield ran the Toll House Inn in Massachusetts.

questions.q: Which frozen treat was invented by an 11-year-old who left a drink with a stirring stick outside on a cold night?
questions.fact: Frank Epperson made his discovery in 1905 and patented it years later.

questions.q: The sandwich is named after an English noble with what title?
questions.fact: The story says the Earl wanted a meal he could eat with one hand while playing cards.

questions.q: Where did ice cream cones become famous in 1904?
choices: A New York hot dog stand
questions.fact: One story says an ice cream seller ran out of dishes and a waffle seller next door rolled up cones.

questions.q: Cotton candy, also called fairy floss, was co-invented in 1897 by someone with which job?
questions.fact: William Morrison, a dentist, created a cotton candy machine with a candy maker.

questions.q: Which famous fizzy drink was invented by a pharmacist in Atlanta in 1886?
questions.fact: John Pemberton first sold it as a medicine-like drink at a pharmacy soda fountain.

questions.q: Ketchup is thought to come from a sauce in Asia made from what?
questions.fact: Tomatoes were added to ketchup much later, in the 1800s.

questions.q: What are the two main ingredients in mayonnaise?
questions.fact: The egg yolk helps the oil and liquid mix smoothly instead of separating.

questions.q: What is soy sauce made from?
questions.fact: Soy sauce has been made in China for more than 2,000 years.

questions.q: Which spicy chili sauce is named after a town in Thailand?
questions.fact: The town is called Si Racha, on the coast of the Gulf of Thailand.

questions.q: What does the Spanish word "salsa" mean?
questions.fact: In English, salsa usually means a tomato and chili sauce, but in Spanish it can mean any sauce.

questions.q: Which spice is the most expensive in the world by weight?
questions.fact: Saffron threads are picked by hand from crocus flowers, and each flower has only three.

questions.q: Vanilla comes from the seed pods of which kind of plant?
questions.fact: Most vanilla orchids are pollinated by hand, one flower at a time.

questions.q: What is black pepper made from?
questions.fact: Black, white and green peppercorns all come from the same plant.

questions.q: Which spice gives curry its bright yellow color?
questions.fact: Turmeric is a root, related to ginger.

questions.q: Which two spices come from the same fruit of one tree?
questions.fact: Nutmeg is the seed, and mace is the lacy red covering around it.

questions.q: What are cloves, the spice?
questions.fact: Cloves are so strong that dentists once used clove oil to numb toothaches.

questions.q: Which part of the ginger plant do we usually eat?
questions.fact: It looks like a root, but ginger is really an underground stem called a rhizome.

questions.q: What is used to measure how spicy a chili pepper is?
questions.fact: A sweet bell pepper scores zero on the Scoville scale.

questions.q: Which chemical makes chili peppers taste hot?
questions.fact: Drinking milk helps with chili burn better than water does.

questions.q: As of 2025, which pepper holds the record as the world's hottest?
questions.fact: Pepper X was named the world's hottest pepper by Guinness World Records in 2023.

questions.q: Which spice is made by drying and grinding red peppers and is popular in Hungary?
questions.fact: Paprika can be sweet, hot or smoked.

questions.q: What is a single piece of a garlic bulb called?
questions.fact: A garlic bulb usually has about 10 to 20 cloves.

questions.q: Which herb is a main ingredient in pesto and is common in Italian cooking?
questions.fact: Basil is part of the mint family.

questions.q: Which herb, loved by some and said to taste like soap to others, is also called coriander?
questions.fact: Some people's genes make cilantro taste soapy to them.

questions.q: Which seeds are ground to make tahini?
questions.fact: Tahini is one of the main ingredients in hummus.

questions.q: Which islands in Indonesia were famous as the Spice Islands?
questions.fact: European traders once sailed halfway around the world for the nutmeg and cloves grown there.

questions.q: Which of these is a true berry, according to botanists?
questions.fact: Botanically, strawberries and raspberries aren't true berries, but bananas, grapes and even tomatoes are.

questions.q: How does a pineapple grow?
choices: From the middle of a leafy plant on the ground
questions.fact: A pineapple plant usually takes about two years to grow one pineapple.

questions.q: Which spiky fruit from Southeast Asia is so smelly it's banned on some trains and in some hotels?
questions.fact: Durian is often called the king of fruits.

questions.q: What grows on the bottom of a fruit called a cashew apple?
questions.fact: Cashews are always sold shelled, because their shells contain an oil that irritates skin.

questions.q: Almonds are the seeds of a fruit closely related to which fruit?
questions.fact: Almonds, peaches, cherries and plums are all in the same plant family.

questions.q: Which fruit was renamed after a New Zealand bird?
questions.fact: Kiwifruit came from China, where it was once called the Chinese gooseberry.

questions.q: Which banana variety is the one most often sold in grocery stores?
questions.fact: Cavendish bananas are grown from cuttings, so they are almost all genetic copies of each other.

questions.q: Why do apples float in water?
choices: They are about a quarter air
questions.fact: That's why bobbing for apples works.

questions.q: Granny Smith and Fuji are types of which fruit?
questions.fact: Granny Smith apples were first grown by a woman named Maria Ann Smith in Australia in the 1860s.

questions.q: Which fruit is the national fruit of India?
questions.fact: India grows more mangoes than any other country.

questions.q: Prunes are dried versions of which fruit?
questions.fact: It takes about three pounds of fresh plums to make one pound of prunes.

questions.q: Pickles are usually made from which vegetable?
questions.fact: Pickling in salty or vinegary water has kept food from spoiling for thousands of years.

questions.q: In which part of the world were potatoes first grown?
choices: The Andes mountains of South America
questions.fact: People in Peru have grown potatoes for more than 7,000 years.

questions.q: Tomatoes first came from which part of the world?
questions.fact: Italian food had no tomatoes until they arrived from the Americas in the 1500s.

questions.q: Corn was first grown thousands of years ago in which country?
questions.fact: Corn was bred from a wild grass called teosinte, which had tiny cobs.

questions.q: What color were most cultivated carrots before orange carrots became common?
questions.fact: Orange carrots became popular in the Netherlands in the 1600s.

questions.q: Broccoli, cabbage, kale and cauliflower were all bred from which wild plant?
questions.fact: Farmers chose different parts to grow bigger, like leaves for kale and flower buds for broccoli.

questions.q: Which part of the rhubarb plant should you never eat?
questions.fact: Rhubarb leaves contain a lot of oxalic acid, which can make people sick.

questions.q: Which vegetable is named after a city in Belgium?
questions.fact: Brussels sprouts look like tiny cabbages, and they're related to cabbages too.

questions.q: Which rare fungi, found underground, are often sniffed out by dogs or pigs?
questions.fact: Some white truffles have sold for thousands of dollars each.

questions.q: Which grain is the main food for more than half of the world's people?
questions.fact: Rice is grown on every continent except Antarctica.

questions.q: Quinoa, a popular healthy food, comes from which mountain region?
questions.fact: Quinoa is actually a seed, not a true grain.

questions.q: Which protein in wheat makes dough stretchy?
questions.fact: People with celiac disease can't eat gluten.

questions.q: Which small, flat legumes are used to make the Indian dish dal?
questions.fact: Lentils cook quickly and don't need soaking like many dried beans do.

questions.q: What is another name for chickpeas?
questions.fact: Chickpeas have been grown in the Middle East for about 10,000 years.

questions.q: As of 2025, which country produces the most olive oil?
questions.fact: Spain often makes nearly half of the world's olive oil.

questions.q: Why have archaeologists found honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that was still safe to eat?
choices: It was kept in gold jars
questions.fact: Honey is low in water and slightly acidic, so germs can't grow in it.

questions.q: About how many liters of maple sap are boiled down to make one liter of maple syrup?
questions.fact: Canada, especially Quebec, makes most of the world's maple syrup.

questions.q: Table sugar mostly comes from which two plants?
questions.fact: Sugarcane is a giant tropical grass that can grow taller than a basketball hoop.

questions.q: What gas do baking soda and baking powder release to make cakes rise?
questions.fact: The gas makes tiny bubbles in the batter that get trapped as it bakes.

questions.q: Which plant root is used to make tapioca?
questions.fact: Cassava must be cooked properly, because raw cassava can contain harmful chemicals.

questions.q: Which fruit is about 92 percent water?
questions.fact: Watermelons are related to cucumbers, pumpkins and squash.

questions.q: On long voyages, sailors ate citrus fruit to prevent which disease?
questions.fact: British sailors were nicknamed "limeys" because they were given lime juice.

questions.q: Which fruit is famous for being high in potassium?
questions.fact: Bananas are also a good source of quick energy for athletes.

questions.q: Which red berries are harvested by flooding the fields so the berries float?
questions.fact: Good cranberries bounce, and some farms test them by bouncing them.

questions.q: In which country did the wild ancestors of today's apples come from?
questions.fact: The name of Kazakhstan's biggest city, Almaty, is linked to the word for apple.

questions.q: What color is a bell pepper before it ripens?
questions.fact: Red bell peppers are usually just green peppers left on the plant longer to ripen.

questions.q: An ear of corn almost always has an even number of what?
questions.fact: Most ears of corn have about 16 rows of kernels.

questions.q: In the 1800s, many Europeans feared which fruit might be poisonous?
questions.fact: Some plates were made with lead, and acidic tomatoes pulled lead out, which may have made people sick.

questions.q: Which mold gives blue cheese its blue veins?
questions.fact: It's related to the mold that the medicine penicillin was first made from.

questions.q: What is the Hawaiian dish poke made from?
questions.fact: Poke means "to slice" or "cut crosswise" in Hawaiian.

questions.q: Which plant gives us the sweet, starchy staple that Hawaiians mash into poi?
questions.fact: Taro leaves are also eaten, but they must be cooked first.

questions.q: What is the edible part of an artichoke?
questions.fact: If an artichoke is left to bloom, it turns into a big purple flower.

questions.q: Which green fruit has the nickname "alligator pear"?
questions.fact: Its bumpy green skin looks a bit like alligator skin.

questions.q: Which tropical fruit has bright pink skin and white or red flesh with tiny black seeds?
questions.fact: Dragon fruit grows on a kind of cactus.

questions.q: Coconuts grow on which kind of tree?
questions.fact: A coconut can float across oceans and sprout on a faraway beach.

questions.q: What are the holes in Swiss cheese called?
questions.fact: The holes form when bacteria in the cheese give off gas as it ages.

questions.q: Which cheese, named after a village in England, is often dyed orange?
questions.fact: The orange color usually comes from annatto, a natural dye from a tree seed.

questions.q: How is yogurt made?
questions.fact: The bacteria turn milk sugar into lactic acid, which makes yogurt thick and tangy.

questions.q: What is ghee, used a lot in Indian cooking?
questions.fact: Ghee is butter that has been cooked to remove the water and milk solids.

questions.q: What decides whether a chicken's eggs are brown or white?
questions.fact: Brown and white eggs have the same taste and nutrition.

questions.q: How can you tell a very fresh egg in a bowl of water?
questions.fact: Older eggs have a bigger air pocket inside, so they start to tilt up or float.

questions.q: What is caviar?
questions.fact: The most famous caviar comes from sturgeon, a fish that has been around since the time of the dinosaurs.

questions.q: Which squeaky cheese from Cyprus is great for grilling because it doesn't melt easily?
questions.fact: Halloumi squeaks against your teeth when you chew it.

questions.q: What is paneer?
choices: A fresh cheese used in Indian cooking
questions.fact: Paneer doesn't melt when heated, so it's often cubed and cooked in curries.

questions.q: What does the name of the Italian cheese ricotta mean?
questions.fact: Ricotta is made by heating the whey left over from making other cheeses.

questions.q: What is sashimi?
choices: Thin slices of raw fish without rice
questions.fact: Sushi always includes vinegared rice, but sashimi doesn't.

questions.q: What sea animal is calamari made from?
questions.fact: Calamari is the Italian word for squid.

questions.q: Bacon usually comes from which part of a pig?
questions.fact: In the UK, back bacon from the pig's back is also very common.

questions.q: What is deer meat called?
questions.fact: The word venison once meant any meat from hunted animals.

questions.q: What is beef jerky?
questions.fact: The word jerky comes from a Quechua word, ch'arki, from South America.

questions.q: Which pizza topping is an American creation, even though it sounds Italian?
questions.fact: As of 2025, pepperoni is the most popular pizza topping in the United States.

questions.q: Which Italian ham is dry-cured and sliced paper thin?
questions.fact: Prosciutto di Parma is cured for at least a year.

questions.q: Which canned meat is so popular in Hawaii that it's used in sushi-like snacks called musubi?
questions.fact: Hawaii eats more Spam per person than any other US state.

questions.q: What does "al dente" mean when cooking pasta?
questions.fact: Al dente is Italian for "to the tooth".

questions.q: What does it mean to sauté food?
choices: Fry it quickly in a little fat
questions.fact: Sauté comes from a French word meaning "to jump", because the food jumps in the hot pan.

questions.q: What does it mean to cut vegetables julienne?
questions.fact: Julienne carrots are often used in salads and stir-fries.

questions.q: What does the French cooking phrase "mise en place" mean?
questions.fact: Chefs prepare and measure all their ingredients before they start cooking.

questions.q: What is blanching vegetables?
choices: Boiling them briefly, then cooling them in ice water
questions.fact: Blanching helps vegetables keep their bright color.

questions.q: What is it called when sugar is heated until it turns brown and tasty?
questions.fact: Caramel starts to form at around 170 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: What is the browning reaction that gives toast, roasted meat and cookies their tasty flavor?
questions.fact: It's named after Louis-Camille Maillard, a French scientist who described it in 1912.

questions.q: What is sous vide cooking?
choices: Cooking sealed food in a warm water bath
questions.fact: Sous vide means "under vacuum" in French.

questions.q: What is a roux, used to thicken sauces?
questions.fact: Gumbo often starts with a dark roux cooked until it's the color of chocolate.

questions.q: How many "mother sauces" are there in classic French cooking?
questions.fact: The five mother sauces are béchamel, velouté, espagnole, tomato and hollandaise.

questions.q: Which classic French white sauce is made from milk, butter and flour?
questions.fact: Béchamel is used in many lasagna and macaroni and cheese recipes.

questions.q: What is the tall white hat worn by chefs called?
questions.fact: Legend says the 100 pleats on a toque stand for 100 ways to cook an egg.

questions.q: What does "sous chef" mean in a kitchen?
choices: The second in charge under the head chef
questions.fact: Sous means "under" in French.

questions.q: What is the highest number of Michelin stars a restaurant can get?
questions.fact: The Michelin Guide was started by a tire company in 1900 to encourage people to drive more.

questions.q: What is the savory "fifth taste", found in foods like mushrooms, cheese and soy sauce?
questions.fact: A Japanese scientist named Kikunae Ikeda named umami in 1908.

questions.q: What is a wok?
choices: A round-bottomed pan used for stir-frying
questions.fact: A wok's shape lets food be tossed quickly over very high heat.

questions.q: What is a tandoor?
questions.fact: Tandoors can get hotter than 400 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: In Japan, why is it rude to stand chopsticks upright in a bowl of rice?
choices: It looks like an offering at a funeral
questions.fact: Passing food from chopsticks to chopsticks is also avoided for the same reason.

questions.q: Why does a pressure cooker cook food faster?
choices: It raises the boiling point of water
questions.fact: Inside a pressure cooker, water can reach about 120 degrees Celsius before boiling.

questions.q: Why do people add salt to the ice when making homemade ice cream?
choices: It keeps the bag from leaking
It stops the ice from melting at all
questions.fact: Salty ice water can get several degrees below the normal freezing point.

questions.q: What dessert is made by whipping egg whites and sugar into a stiff foam and baking it?
questions.fact: A copper bowl helps egg whites whip into a more stable foam.

questions.q: Which seaweed-based ingredient is used as a vegetarian replacement for gelatin?
questions.fact: Agar sets firm even at room temperature.

questions.q: What is the process of heating milk to kill germs called?
questions.fact: It's named after the French scientist Louis Pasteur.

questions.q: What are the colorful French cookies made from almond flour and meringue called?
questions.fact: Macaroons, with two O's, are a different cookie usually made with coconut.

questions.q: What does the name of the dessert crème brûlée mean?
questions.fact: The top is covered with sugar and burned with a small torch to make a crunchy crust.

questions.q: What is mochi?
choices: A Japanese rice cake made from pounded sticky rice
questions.fact: Mochi is pounded with big wooden mallets in a ceremony called mochitsuki.

questions.q: Which three flavors make up Neapolitan ice cream?
questions.fact: It's named after Naples, Italy, the hometown of the immigrants who made layered ice cream popular in the US.

questions.q: What three things make a classic s'more?
questions.fact: The name s'more comes from "some more", because people always want another one.

questions.q: Marshmallows were first made from the root of which plant?
questions.fact: Ancient Egyptians made a honey treat with mallow root sap.

questions.q: Which company invented the first gummy bears, in Germany in 1922?
questions.fact: Haribo's name comes from its founder, Hans Riegel, and the city of Bonn.

questions.q: In which country were fortune cookies most likely invented?
questions.fact: Fortune cookies are rarely served in China, and they are probably based on a Japanese cracker.

questions.q: In which US city were brownies said to be first made, in 1893?
questions.fact: The first brownies were made at the Palmer House Hotel for the World's Columbian Exposition.

questions.q: Which kind of chocolate contains no cocoa solids at all?
questions.fact: White chocolate is made from cocoa butter, sugar and milk.

questions.q: In which country was milk chocolate invented, in 1875?
questions.fact: Daniel Peter worked with his neighbor, Henri Nestlé, to get the milk just right.

questions.q: As of 2025, which country is usually ranked as eating the most chocolate per person?
questions.fact: People in Switzerland eat around 10 kilograms of chocolate each per year.

questions.q: What did the Aztecs sometimes use cacao beans as?
questions.fact: Aztec chocolate drinks were bitter and spicy, not sweet.

questions.q: In which country was tea first drunk?
questions.fact: A legend says a leaf fell into an emperor's hot water about 5,000 years ago.

questions.q: According to legend, who discovered coffee after noticing his animals got very energetic?
questions.fact: The story of the goat herder Kaldi comes from Ethiopia.

questions.q: As of 2025, which country is usually ranked as drinking the most coffee per person?
questions.fact: Finns drink about 12 kilograms of coffee per person each year.

questions.q: What is matcha?
questions.fact: In matcha, you drink the whole ground tea leaf instead of just water soaked with leaves.

questions.q: Bubble tea, with chewy tapioca pearls, was invented in which place?
questions.fact: Bubble tea became popular in Taiwan in the 1980s.
